- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and price drops, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid under-shock.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights short-term momentum; if sentiment is volatile, reduce forecast slope by 20–40% to reflect uncertainty.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with true momentum.
